existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No charge for re-redacting previously redacted record
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge for redaction labor if it knows or has reason to know it previously redacted the record and the redacted version is still in its possession.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body previously redacted the same record and retains the redacted version.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body shall not charge for labor directly associated with redaction under section 14 if it knows or has reason to know that it previously redacted the public record in question and the redacted version is still in the public body's possession.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Fee limited to actual incremental cost
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A permitted fee is limited to actual mailing costs and the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication, including labor and the cost of search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material, and the total must not exceed the sum of the six enumerated components.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body charges or estimates a fee.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: sum of the 6 enumerated components (actual incremental cost)
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the fee must be limited to actual mailing costs, and to the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication including labor, the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14. Except as otherwise provided in this act, if the public body estimates or charges a fee in accordance with this act, the total fee must not exceed the sum of the following components:
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Umbrella fee-cap; the six components are MI-0034/0036/0037/0038/0039/0040.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Search labor rate — lowest-paid capable employee
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Labor for searching, locating, and examining records may not be charged at more than the hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of doing so, regardless of who performs the labor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body charges search/location/examination labor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of searching for, locating, and examining the public records in the particular instance regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Labor charged in 15-minute increments, rounded down
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Search/examination labor costs must be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body charges search/examination labor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: fixed: 15-minute increments, partial increments rounded down
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Labor costs under this subdivision shall be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Same increment rule also applies to redaction labor under (1)(b); duplication labor (1)(e) allows increments of the body's choosing rounded down.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Redaction/separation labor rate ceiling
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Labor to separate/delete exempt from nonexempt information may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid capable employee; if none is employed, contracted labor may be charged like employee labor but not exceeding 6 times the state minimum hourly wage.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body charges separation/deletion (redaction) labor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: lowest-paid capable employee wage; contracted labor <= 6x state minimum hourly wage
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: For services performed by an employee of the public body, the public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of separating and deleting exempt information from nonexempt information in the particular instance... Total labor costs calculated under this subdivision for contracted labor costs must not exceed an amount equal to 6 times the state minimum hourly wage rate determined under section 4 of the improved workforce opportunity wage act, 2018 PA 337, MCL 408.934.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Contracted-labor ceiling references a moving external figure (state minimum wage).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Nonpaper physical media at actual economical cost
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For records provided on nonpaper physical media, the charge is limited to the actual and most reasonably economical cost of that media.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Records provided on nonpaper physical media.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual most-economical cost of the nonpaper media
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: For public records provided to the requestor on any form of nonpaper physical media, the actual and most reasonably economical cost of the nonpaper physical media.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Does not apply if the body lacks the technological capability for the stipulated media.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Paper copy charge ceiling — 10 cents per sheet
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The charge for paper copies must not exceed 10 cents per sheet for copies made on 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper, calculated as a total cost per sheet.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body provides paper copies.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper. A public body shall utilize the most economical means available for making copies of public records, including using double-sided printing, if cost saving and available.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Shared per-page copy-rate ceiling key. Excludes labor (which is separately capped).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Duplication/publication labor rate ceiling
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Labor directly associated with duplication or publication (paper or digital copies, transfers) may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid employee capable of the duplication.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body charges duplication/publication labor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee; increments of body's choosing, rounded down
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of necessary duplication or publication in the particular instance, regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor. Labor costs under this subdivision may be estimated and charged in time increments of the public body's choosing; however, all partial time increments shall be rounded down.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Actual mailing cost only
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Mailing may be charged at actual cost in a reasonably economical manner; no charge for expedited shipping or insurance unless stipulated by the requester.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body mails records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of least-expensive economical mailing (plus delivery confirmation)
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The actual cost of mailing, if any, for sending the public records in a reasonably economical and justifiable manner. The public body shall not charge more for expedited shipping or insurance unless specifically stipulated by the requestor, but may otherwise charge for the least expensive form of postal delivery confirmation when mailing public records.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Up to 50% fringe-benefit add-on to labor
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge to cover fringe benefits, not exceeding the actual cost of fringe benefits, if it notes the multiplier on the itemization.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body charges labor and elects to recover fringe benefits.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: +50% of the applicable labor charge (capped at actual fringe cost)
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The public body may also add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge amount to cover or partially cover the cost of fringe benefits if it clearly notes the percentage multiplier used to account for benefits in the detailed itemization described in subsection (4). Subject to the 50% limitation, the public body shall not charge more than the actual cost of fringe benefits, and overtime wages shall not be used in calculating the cost of fringe benefits.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: A higher multiplier is allowed only in the narrow website-then-paper scenario under § 15.234(5).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Overtime excluded from labor unless stipulated
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Overtime wages may not be included in labor-cost calculations unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requester and noted on the itemization.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Labor performed on overtime.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Overtime wages shall not be included in the calculation of labor costs unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requestor and clearly noted on the detailed itemization described in subsection (4).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: First $20 free for indigent / designated nonprofit
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A record search and copies must be furnished without charge for the first $20 of the fee for each request by a qualifying indigent individual (with affidavit) or by a state-designated developmental-disabilities/mental-illness protection-and-advocacy nonprofit.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester is a qualifying indigent individual or a qualifying designated nonprofit.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: fixed: first $20.00 of the fee waived per request
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public record search shall be made and a copy of a public record shall be furnished without charge for the first $20.00 of the fee for each request by either of the following: (a) An individual who is entitled to information under this act and who submits an affidavit stating that the individual is indigent and receiving specific public assistance or, if not receiving public assistance, stating facts showing inability to pay the cost because of indigency.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Indigent ineligible if already received the discount twice that calendar year from the same body, or if request is in conjunction with paying outside parties. Nonprofit conditions in § 15.234(2)(b).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Discretionary public-interest fee waiver/reduction
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may search for or furnish copies without charge or at a reduced charge if it determines a waiver/reduction is in the public interest because the disclosure primarily benefits the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body determines disclosure primarily benefits the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A search for a public record may be conducted or copies of public records may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge if the public body determines that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because searching for or furnishing copies of the public record can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Discretionary; 'public interest / primarily benefiting the general public' is a soft standard.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Search/redaction labor chargeable only if not charging would cause unreasonably high costs
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A fee for search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material may not be charged unless failure to charge would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request, and the body specifically identifies the nature of those costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body wishes to charge search/examination/review/separation labor.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A fee as described in subsection (1) shall not be charged for the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14 unless failure to charge a fee would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request in the particular instance, and the public body specifically identifies the nature of these unreasonably high costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: A gate the engine must evaluate before charging labor components; structural condition, not a value.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No charge for records already on the body's website
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Public records available to the general public on the body's website at the time of the request are exempt from separation/deletion labor charges under (1)(b).
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requested records are available on the body's public website when the request is made.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If the public body directly or indirectly administers or maintains an official internet presence, any public records available to the general public on that internet site at the time the request is made are exempt from any charges under subsection (1)(b).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Standard itemized fee form
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body's procedures must use a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee that clearly lists and explains the allowable charges for each of the six fee components used in estimating or charging.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body estimates or charges a fee.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body's procedures and guidelines must include the use of a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee amount in its responses to written requests under this act. The detailed itemization must clearly list and explain the allowable charges for each of the 6 fee components listed under subsection (1) that compose the total fee used for estimating or charging purposes.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: DTMB provides a model form; a body may create its own compliant form.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Procedures, guidelines, and written public summary
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body must establish procedures and guidelines to implement the act and create a written public summary (how to submit requests, understand responses, deposits, fee calculations, and appeals), post them on any website, and provide free copies with responses and on request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body is subject to the act.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body shall establish procedures and guidelines to implement this act and shall create a written public summary of the specific procedures and guidelines relevant to the general public regarding how to submit written requests to the public body and explaining how to understand a public body's written responses, deposit requirements, fee calculations, and avenues for challenge and appeal.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Procedures/guidelines are themselves non-exempt public records.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: No fees/deposits until procedures published
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, created a written public summary, or made them publicly available free may not require deposits or charge fees until it is in compliance.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body lacks published procedures/guidelines/summary.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, has not created a written public summary, or has not made those items publicly available without charge as required in this subsection is not relieved of its duty to comply with any requirement of this act and shall not require deposits or charge fees otherwise permitted under this act until it is in compliance with this subsection.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: 5%-per-day labor-fee reduction for late response
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If a public body does not respond timely and the lateness was willful/intentional or the request was flagged, it must reduce labor-cost charges by 5% for each day it exceeds the response deadline, up to a 50% maximum reduction.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Untimely response AND (willful/intentional) OR (request carried FOIA flagging language/keywords).
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: fixed: -5% of labor charge per late day, capped at -50%
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Reduce the charges for labor costs otherwise permitted under this section by 5% for each day the public body exceeds the time permitted under section 5(2) for a response to the request, with a maximum 50% reduction, if either of the following applies: (i) The late response was willful and intentional. (ii) The written request included language that conveyed a request for information within the first 250 words of the body of a letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or electronic mail attachment, or specifically included the words, characters, or abbreviations for "freedom of information", "information", "FOIA", "copy", or a recognizable misspelling of such, or appropriate legal code reference for this act, on the front of an envelope, or in the subject line of an electronic mail, letter, or facsimile cover page.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Fee-calculation remedy tied to lateness; reduces only the labor components.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Fee section inapplicable to statutorily-priced records
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The fee section does not apply to records prepared under a statute specifically authorizing their sale, or where another act/statute specifically sets the copy fee.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requested record has a statutorily-authorized sale price or a specifically-provided copy fee.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: This section does not apply to public records prepared under an act or statute specifically authorizing the sale of those public records to the public, or if the amount of the fee for providing a copy of the public record is otherwise specifically provided by an act or statute.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Good-faith deposit permitted above $50
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may require a good-faith deposit before providing records if the entire estimated fee or charge exceeds $50, based on a good-faith total-fee calculation.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Good-faith fee estimate exceeds $50.00.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: floor: deposit only allowed when estimate exceeds $50.00
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: the public body may require a good-faith deposit from the person requesting information before providing the public records to the requestor if the entire fee estimate or charge authorized under this section exceeds $50.00, based on a good-faith calculation of the total fee described in subsection (4).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Deposit capped at one-half of estimate
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A good-faith deposit must not exceed one-half of the total estimated fee, and the deposit request must include a detailed fee itemization.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body requires a good-faith deposit under § 15.234(8).
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: 1/2 of the total estimated fee
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Subject to subsection (10), the deposit must not exceed 1/2 of the total estimated fee, and a public body's request for a deposit must include a detailed itemization as required under subsection (4).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Up to 100% deposit for prior non-payers
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a subsequent request from an individual who did not pay in full for a prior fulfilled request, the body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before beginning the search, if six enumerated conditions are all met.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Individual left a prior granted-and-fulfilled request unpaid and the six conditions in § 15.234(11)(a)-(f) are all satisfied.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: up to 100% of estimated fee (only when all six conditions met, incl. 90 days since availability notice)
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: after a public body has granted and fulfilled a written request from an individual under this act, if the public body has not been paid in full the total amount under subsection (1)...the public body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before it begins a full public record search for any subsequent written request from that individual if all of the following apply:
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Conditions include: prior final fee <=105% of estimate; records still in possession; 90 days since availability notice; no proof of prior payment; detailed itemization. Structural branch with a parameter ceiling.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Termination of 100% deposit authority
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The body must stop requiring the increased (up to 100%) deposit if the individual shows proof of prior full payment, the body is later paid in full, or 365 days have passed since the unpaid request was made.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Proof of payment shown, prior request paid in full, or 365 days elapsed since the unpaid request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: terminal: 365 days from the unpaid written request extinguishes the increased-deposit authority
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body shall no longer require an increased estimated fee deposit from an individual as described under subsection (11) if any of the following apply: (a) The individual is able to show proof of prior payment in full to the public body. (b) The public body is subsequently paid in full for the applicable prior written request. (c) Three hundred sixty-five days have passed since the individual made the written request for which full payment was not remitted to the public body.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Request abandoned if deposit unpaid within 45 days
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: If a required deposit is not received within 45 days after the requester's receipt of the deposit notice, and no deposit-amount appeal was filed, the request is considered abandoned and the body need no longer fulfill it.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Deposit not received within 45 days of receipt of the deposit notice and no § 15.240a appeal filed.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: terminal: 45 days from requester's receipt of the deposit notice
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If a deposit that is required under subsection (8) or (11) is not received by the public body within 45 days from receipt by the requesting person of the notice that a deposit is required, and if the requesting person has not filed an appeal of the deposit amount pursuant to section 10a, the request shall be considered abandoned by the requesting person and the public body is no longer required to fulfill the request.

fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: The charge for paper copies must not exceed 10 cents per sheet for copies made on 8.5x11 or 8.5x14 paper, calculated as a total cost per sheet.

fee.labor_charge.summary: Labor for searching, locating, and examining records may not be charged at more than the hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of doing so, regardless of who performs the labor.
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee

fee.labor_charge.summary: Search/examination labor costs must be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: fixed: 15-minute increments, partial increments rounded down

fee.labor_charge.summary: Labor to separate/delete exempt from nonexempt information may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid capable employee; if none is employed, contracted labor may be charged like employee labor but not exceeding 6 times the state minimum hourly wage.
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: lowest-paid capable employee wage; contracted labor <= 6x state minimum hourly wage

fee.labor_charge.summary: Labor directly associated with duplication or publication (paper or digital copies, transfers) may not exceed the hourly wage of the lowest-paid employee capable of the duplication.
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee; increments of body's choosing, rounded down

fee.labor_charge.summary: A public body may add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge to cover fringe benefits, not exceeding the actual cost of fringe benefits, if it notes the multiplier on the itemization.
fee.labor_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: +50% of the applicable labor charge (capped at actual fringe cost)

fee.labor_charge.summary: Overtime wages may not be included in labor-cost calculations unless overtime is specifically stipulated by the requester and noted on the itemization.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: A permitted fee is limited to actual mailing costs and the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication, including labor and the cost of search, examination, review, and separation/deletion of exempt material, and the total must not exceed the sum of the six enumerated components.
fee.actual_cost_basis.clock_spec: ceiling: sum of the 6 enumerated components (actual incremental cost)

fee.electronic_media_charge.summary: For records provided on nonpaper physical media, the charge is limited to the actual and most reasonably economical cost of that media.
fee.electronic_media_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: actual most-economical cost of the nonpaper media

fee.delivery_charge.summary: Mailing may be charged at actual cost in a reasonably economical manner; no charge for expedited shipping or insurance unless stipulated by the requester.
fee.delivery_charge.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost of least-expensive economical mailing (plus delivery confirmation)

fee.no_charge_categories.summary: A public body may not charge for redaction labor if it knows or has reason to know it previously redacted the record and the redacted version is still in its possession.
Public records available to the general public on the body's website at the time of the request are exempt from separation/deletion labor charges under (1)(b).

A public body that has not established procedures and guidelines, created a written public summary, or made them publicly available free may not require deposits or charge fees until it is in compliance.

fee.schedule_and_authority.summary: A public body must establish procedures and guidelines to implement the act and create a written public summary (how to submit requests, understand responses, deposits, fee calculations, and appeals), post them on any website, and provide free copies with responses and on request.
